meta.disclaimer: Veterinary and food-import rules change with disease outbreaks. This is planning guidance only — declare all animal products at the border and follow official notices on the day you cross.
meta.sourceLabel: National veterinary services & border agency notices

intro: Southern Africa protects livestock industries with strict border controls on meat, dairy, and animal products. Self-caterers and campers are most often caught out — finish or discard restricted items before the queue, not at the officer's desk.
generalRules: Declare all meat, dairy, honey, and pet food — even leftovers from yesterday's braai
Commercially sealed tins and long-life UHT products are usually tolerated; fresh and frozen items are not
Botswana is the strictest — plan a supermarket stop after crossing, not before
Pet dogs and cats need import permits and vaccination records — arrange weeks ahead
Hunting trophies and skins require CITES permits and vet certificates

countries.name: Botswana
banned: Fresh, frozen, or chilled meat and poultry
Milk, cheese, butter, and other unpasteurised dairy
Raw honey and untreated animal products
usuallyAllowed: Sealed tins of meat and fish
Dry packaged snacks without meat ingredients
countries.borderPosts: All land borders — Martin's Drift, Kazungula, Ramokgwebana, Ngoma
countries.penalty: Confiscation and possible fine; delays if undeclared
countries.tip: Stock up at Gaborone, Maun, or Kasane supermarkets after entry.

countries.name: South Africa
banned: Meat and dairy from FMD-affected zones without permits
usuallyAllowed: Sealed retail products from reputable suppliers
countries.borderPosts: All international land borders; OR Tambo agricultural inspection for some flights
countries.penalty: Confiscation; biosecurity fines for commercial quantities
countries.tip: Returning from Botswana or Zimbabwe — discard fresh meat before re-entering SA if unsure of origin.

countries.name: Namibia
banned: Fresh meat from outside SACU without veterinary certificate
usuallyAllowed: SACU-origin sealed retail meat (South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho, Eswatini)
countries.penalty: Confiscation at discretion of veterinary officer
countries.tip: SACU harmonised rules apply between member states — still declare at the post.

countries.name: Zambia
banned: Products without valid veterinary import permit (commercial)
countries.penalty: Confiscation; commercial imports need prior permit
countries.tip: KAZA tourists often carry snacks — declare rather than hide.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
banned: Dairy from non-approved sources during outbreak periods
usuallyAllowed: Sealed retail products in personal quantities
Tinned and dried camping food if declared
countries.tip: Victoria Falls supermarkets stock everything — buy after crossing if unsure.

countries.name: Mozambique
usuallyAllowed: Personal camping supplies in sealed packaging
Dry goods and tins if declared
countries.penalty: Confiscation; delays at busy Lebombo if undeclared
countries.tip: Maputo supermarkets well stocked — discard SA braai leftovers before Lebombo.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.tip: Entering from Zambia — similar rules; declare honey and biltong.

countries.name: Lesotho
usuallyAllowed: Personal food for mountain trips if declared
countries.borderPosts: Maseru Bridge, Sani Pass, Caledonspoort, Ficksburg
countries.penalty: Rare for tourists — confiscation if commercial quantities
countries.tip: Remote highlands have no shops — pack sealed non-perishables legally.

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.tip: SACU rules align with South Africa — still answer honestly if asked.
